desc: Prove the prefix-maximum cost formula and the two monotonicity properties (fixed l: cost non-decreasing in r; fixed r: cost non-increasing as l grows) justifying the two-pointer scan.
Verify the chain-query design and two-pointer counting by hand on both examples (17 and 12 reproduced) and on edge patterns (all equal, strictly increasing/decreasing).

Implement the complete solution: monotonic-stack next-strictly-greater, binary-lifting tables (ancestors + segment running-max sums, sentinel index n), O(log n) `cost(l,r)` query, two-pointer count adding `r-l+1` per l.

Validate against a brute-force O(n²) checker on small random arrays, covering equal values, strictly increasing/decreasing, single element, minimal k, and very large values/costs; both provided examples pass (2000+ fuzz trials matched).
Memory/time optimization: lifting tables already use `array('i')`/`array('q')` (~20 MB); n=10^5 adversarial inputs complete within limits — no further work needed.
